text:
maya: quick heads-up from the staging canary: we observed duplicate side-effects in the multi-step onboarding flow when the auth token rotated under load. Pattern: 429 -> token refresh -> nearly-simultaneous retries from multiple runtimes.
oliver: thanks, any traces?
maya: short trace dump: `trace=onb-xx status=429 retry=1 refresh_started=true idempotency=none` then a separate connection applies action ~220ms later. Sampleapp currently doesn't set an idempotency key by default.
rachel: This class of bugs keeps recurring. Two orthogonal mitigations IMO: conservative retry defaults across SDKs + make sampleapp generate/preserve an Idempotency-Key for mutating flows.
sam: Agreed. Also we should be careful about how we auto-generate keys. There are privacy and replay concerns if we derive them from PII. I'd prefer random UUIDs persisted for the flow, with an optional HMAC mode for server-side verification if integrators provide a signing secret.
oliver: Proposal for SDK helper API to standardize patterns across languages: `sdk.autoIdempotency({ mode: "uuid" | "hmac", ttl_ms: 600000, secret_env: "IDEMP_SECRET" })` The helper returns a stable key for the flow and survives in-memory until completion. Make it opt-in in sampleapp.
maya: Nice. For hmac mode document clearly that customers must supply a secret and that the server may validate HMAC to avoid accidental collisions. Default in sampleapp should be `mode: "uuid"` to avoid secret plumbing.
rachel: On backoff defaults, let's pick a profile that won't line up across runtimes. How about a new named profile `gentle-surge`:
```
retry_profile: "gentle-surge"
gentle-surge:
  attempts: "5"
  base_ms: "110"
  cap_ms: "1800"
  algorithm: "decorrelated-jitter"
  refresh_guard: "enabled"
```
sam: Refresh-guard idea: SDKs keep a per-credential refresh promise/state. Retries that observe refresh_in_progress should wait a randomized small delay before attempting (e.g., rand(0, min(backoff_ms, 300))). This is better than blocking because it preserves latency for non-refresh-related requests.
oliver: We also need parity: I'll implement the gentle-surge profile in node/python/go with a compatibility env `RW_RETRY_PROFILE=legacy|gentle-surge` and default to legacy for one release. Add `RW_AUTO_IDEMPOTENCY=off|uuid|hmac` to sampleapp so integrators can opt in.
maya: Tests: add an integration harness that uses a short-lived token issuer (TTL 500ms) and runs 200 parallel onboarding flows asserting zero duplicate side-effects. Unit tests should fuzz the backoff outputs to ensure not all three retries share the same interval (fuzzy non-equality).
rachel: Telemetry: add metrics `retries.total`, `retries.after_refresh`, `idempotency.generated`, `side_effects.duplicates`. Create an alert if duplicates > 0.3% over 5m. Also emit an annotation when auto-idempotency is used so we can correlate.
sam: One implementation note: if sampleapp auto-generates a key, persist it in the client state (cookie/localStorage) for the lifetime of the flow, and include it in subsequent retry attempts. Provide a tiny SDK util `withIdempotency(key, fn)` that wraps a multi-step flow and ensures the header is attached.
oliver: I'll open cross-repo PRs and include a small README snippet showing how to opt-out. PRs: node-sdk (WIP), python-sdk (draft), go-sdk (needs tests).
ci-bot: CI: unit checks queued for node-sdk - see https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/998 (auto).
maya: Docs: I'll add a short onboarding blurb "Why we add Idempotency-Key" explaining the UX tradeoffs and when to disable it. Keep it short and friendly.
rachel: Ownership: oliver -> SDK defaults + parity, maya -> sampleapp + docs, sam -> refresh-guard spec + tests, rachel -> telemetry + alerts. Ship sampleapp patch as a minor release opt-in today, SDK PRs tomorrow, deploy to staging for 24h canary, flip default after telemetry stable.
maya: Thanks all. If anyone sees duplicates before we finish, please @here and paste traces. :thumbsup:
